name: The Fitting Book
one_line: Naira Petite styled the way its couture house thinks: twelve pages from the Nashik studio's fitting book, where real Naira Flore fabrics, croquis, tailor's tools and pencilled fitting notes decide which piece goes with which thread, neckline, sleeve, dupatta and function this festive and wedding season.
big_idea: Naira is a couture house first (130 of its 140 Instagram posts are couture) that also sells demi-fine jewellery, and until now the two businesses have never spoken to each other on the grid. The Fitting Book makes the jewellery feed the house's own notebook: every post is a numbered page (page one to page twelve) carrying a stitched woven house label, and every page answers a question a couture fitting actually asks before the jewellery is chosen: what thread is the embroidery in, where does the neckline sit, how long is the sleeve, where does the dupatta fall, which function is it for. The answers are house rules that cross-reference each other across the grid (page five's kurta is gold tone because page one says the thread decides the metal; page twelve's sangeet look gets a ring because page nine says full sleeves skip the wrist), so the feed reads as one thought-through system, the way PTAT's MILNI reads as one event. The world is built only from things Naira owns: pinked swatches cut (as photo crops) from real Naira Flore couture pieces, real Naira Petite cut-outs pinned to the page with glass-head dressmaker's pins, pen croquis on pattern paper, the embroidery hoop, the tailor's tape, the thimble, the order book, the trial-room curtain, the dress form and the blush box. Four named series of three run through the twelve pages: FITTING NOTES (big collaged pages: outfit to pieces), PATTERN NOTES (quiet croquis guides: neckline, sleeve, dupatta), WORKTABLE (one tailor's tool, one piece, one exact measured fact, one Indian wink) and THE STUDIO (reels where drawn studio furniture frames real photographs). Maximal in idea and system, premium in execution: one colour field per tile, one tool or one swatch per page, never sticker soup, and the jewellery always the real photograph.
why_it_fits: BRAND: it argues the one thing no demi-fine competitor can copy, that Naira is a real made-to-measure couture house in Nashik (brand bible section 1; upclose PLAN: 'NAIRA is a couture house first, so our jewellery gets styled where the thread is'), while never claiming the jewellery is hand-made: the copy only ever says the outfits are made to measure and the jewellery is Naira Petite, 18K gold tone & rhodium plated. It uses only shipped brand assets (Velista caps, Cormorant italic turns, Jost labels, the NAIRA wordmark once per frame inside the label, the deck watercolour sprig, blush/sage/ivory, the LAC oxblood and the exhibition bottle green) and real couture photography from the site (look-1..7, hero_1..3, about-uniquely-yours). DATA: guides and proof are what this audience saves and buys from: 84% of attributed purchases came from IG feed and story stills (data-meta s1), so 9 of 12 posts are stills or carousels; the buyer is a 35-54 metro woman (64% of purchases) dressing for festive and wedding functions, who needs 'what goes with this blouse' more than mood; physical fact framing won ('THE WIDTH.' 9.6 ATC per Rs1k; 'Woven, not cast'); concept statics beat plain 1.44x vs 0.57x ROAS; the object-rhyme wink won the account's best ad ('Anaar, pre-peeled.', ROAS 4.52); Edition Two's story is metal and stone choice (12 pieces in both metals; Ruby 8 of 13 Baguette Tennis Bracelets sold since 16 Oct); necklaces are the under-sold category (28 of 207 units in 120 days) while the Baguette Tennis Necklace sits at 70 in stock with 0 sold, so two of twelve posts teach necklace length; the couture era's biggest posts ever were process and unboxing (3,149 and 3,410 likes), so the Studio reels show process and the box. Every hero is deep stock (19 to 79 units) and every price is today's roster price. OWNER TASTE: Indian everyday-object wit with restraint ('CHALNI, FOR THE WRIST.', 'MEASUREMENTS: NOT NEEDED.', 'THE THIMBLE COMES OFF AT SIX.'), lilac (P8 ground, P1 and P12 swatches), deck florals as one pressed sprig, moody night grounds (oxblood, bottle green, plum: one dark tile per row on a zigzag), clean plates, exact facts in mm and cm, no black, no sand or beige grounds, no stickers or stamps, no grand copy, no discount art, no faces on product tiles (on-model crops start below the lips), no lyrics on reels. REFERENCE: it takes PTAT rows 3 and 4 literally but in Naira's register: the pen-drawn frame around a real photo (r3c3 wardrobe = our trial-room curtain and dress form), the numbered look list with real cut-outs (r4c1 = our THE LOOK LIST [01]-[05] with real Naira Flore couture figures), the ruled-paper page with cut-outs (r4c2 = our ruled fitting pages), the domestic object as display (r3c2 steel tray = our hoop, tape, thimble, order book), script + caps pairing (Velista caps + Cormorant italic), and the 'vol 1' series promise (FITTING NOTES N° 01, page one of twelve). Like MILNI's lockup, the stitched house label sits in the same place on every tile, so twelve different pages read as one book.

grid_system.type_system: Fonts from kit/tokens.css (link kit/tokens.css then kit/post-base.css). DISPLAY: Velista 400, caps only (unicase), line-height 0.94, letter-spacing .01em; covers 100-168px so every headline reads in the grid at 36% (>= 90px rule); interior slides 84-104px. Velista has NO rupee sign, NO middle dot, NO em dash, NO degree sign and NO square brackets: set 'N°', '[01]', prices and middots in Jost. ASIDE: Cormorant Garamond italic 400, lowercase, 40-56px, the turn under every headline, ends in a full stop. LABELS AND FOLIOS: Jost 500 caps, 20-24px, tracking .30-.32em, #6B625B (light) or #E9D9C6 (dark). SPEC LINES: Jost 400, 24-28px, #6B625B, sentence case, max two lines. PRICES: Jost 400 30-34px #1A1614 with the rupee sign falling back to Poppins (tokens --nf-font-label), only on index slides, never on covers. HANDWRITTEN FITTING NOTES: Kalam 400, 34-44px, graphite #3D3530 (cream #F6EFE6 on dark), rotated -3 to +3 degrees, max three notes per slide, max eight words per note, each with a pencil arrow (SVG cubic path, 2.5px, round caps, open 14px arrowhead, same colour). Kalam is a stand-in for the founder's own hand: the preferred build scans about 60 short notes written by Vandana in graphite on ivory paper (see risks). Never more than these four roles on one slide.
grid_system.emblem_and_recurring_devices: EMBLEM: THE HOUSE LABEL, a woven garment label stitched onto every cover, the way the house sews its label into every outfit. It holds the NAIRA wordmark (kit/naira-wordmark-ink-blush.svg: ink letters, blush flower as the I), so the wordmark appears once per frame and only there. Build (C-LABEL): rect 300x96 px, fill #F6EFE6; weave = horizontal 1px lines #E9D9C6 every 4px at 50% opacity; folded ends = 10px strips #E9D9C6 at left and right; two X-stitches per end (each X 14px, centred 22px in from the edge, stroke #F5A58F 3px, round caps); shadow 0 4px 10px rgba(40,22,10,.18); wordmark 210px wide centred. RECURRING DEVICES (each with one job, never stacked for decoration): (1) C-PIN glass-head dressmaker's pin: shaft 2.5px, linear gradient #8E8984 to #D9D5CF, 120-150px long, at 30-45 degrees; head circle r=11 with radial gradient (blush #FFD9CC to #F5A58F, sage #C8D8D4 to #7F9A91, or gold #F3DDA6 to #B0843A) plus a 3px white highlight upper-left; drop-shadow 0 2px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.25). Every jewellery cut-out and every swatch is held by one pin. (2) C-PINKED swatch: a real couture fabric photo crop with zigzag pinking-shear edges on all four sides (tooth 16px wide, 8px deep, CSS clip-path polygon), shadow 0 10px 22px rgba(40,22,10,.22); only on FITTING NOTES pages. (4) Pen croquis and pattern marks (sage-deep #4F7268 3px line, blush chalk #F5A58F dashed 12/8, notches as 14px triangles, grainline arrows) only on PATTERN NOTES pages. (5) One tailor's tool per WORKTABLE page: the embroidery hoop, the tape measure, the thimble. (6) Drawn studio furniture framing a real photo on THE STUDIO reels: the order pad, the trial-room curtain and mirror, the dress form. (7) The pressed sprig: kit/motifs/botanical/leaf-sprig-2.png (the bag's watercolour vine), one stem only, held by a glassine strip (rect 120x36, rgba(255,255,255,.55), rotated 12 degrees), used at most once per post, only on FITTING NOTES pages. grid_system.transition_to_existing_grid: The newest live row is LAC (oxblood #42060E, cream serif caps) | the black flower on bone #F1EDE4 | BONE (oxblood). The bottom new row sits on it as an inverted checkerboard: P3 ivory pattern paper over LAC, P2 LAC oxblood over the bone flower tile, P1 ivory ruled paper over BONE. So the August campaign's own value rhythm (dark, light, dark) is answered once (light, dark, light) and the two rows lock like a chessboard instead of colliding. P2 reuses LAC's exact oxblood, sampled from the tile (rgb 66,6,14), with gold line work, so the old campaign's colour is carried up into the new book; P2's hoop-moon sits directly above the old flower mark, one circle over one flower. The Velista caps headlines echo LAC and BONE's high-contrast serif caps, so the type voice continues while the content changes from a launch title to useful pages. From row 3 up the grid opens into colour (bottle green, blush, sage, lilac, plum), and the top row is light for the wedding season, so a visitor arriving from an ad sees a fresh, useful, current page first and the August campaign last.
grid_system.pins: No pins during the rollout (27 Oct to 22 Nov), so each week completes one clean row. When posting resumes after P12, either pin nothing or pin the whole top row P12, P11, P10 together (a full row, so alignment never shifts); never pin one or two. posts.concept: The opener states the house's first rule: before a couture house picks jewellery, it looks at the thread. Gold zari takes gold tone, silver thread takes rhodium, both in one border (Ganga-Jamuni) takes two-tone, and no zari at all lets the stones pick their colour from the fabric. The proof is the same Edition Two bangle in both metals, each pinned to a real Naira Flore couture swatch. It is useful on day one and introduces the book, the label and the pins.

posts.caption:
Five functions, five pieces. The wedding season, planned the way a couture house plans a trousseau.

Haldi: brushed gold huggies, no stones for the haldi to settle in. Mehendi: green huggies, hands left free for the henna. Sangeet: full sleeves, so a ring. Shaadi: a V-neck, so the Y-lariat. Reception: one cushion stone in silver tone.

Outfits from Naira Flore couture, made to measure in Nashik. Jewellery from Naira Petite. Page twelve, the last page of this Fitting Book; the other eleven are below.

[ the look list · 18k gold tone and rhodium plated · five functions, no repeats ]

posts.alt_text: On a sage green ground, five small cut-out figures in Naira Flore couture, numbered one to five: a marigold lehenga, a printed patchwork lehenga, a lilac jacket set, a blush lehenga embroidered with trees and a blush draped saree gown. A small piece of jewellery is pinned beside each. The headline reads The Look List, with haldi, mehendi, sangeet, shaadi, reception beneath it.
posts.why: The top-left tile is the first thing ad traffic sees through the December muhurats (2-6 and 11-12 Dec), so it must be the most useful, most Naira page: real couture (130 of 140 posts are couture) meeting real jewellery, which no demi-fine competitor can show. Women 35-54 (64% of purchases) dress as wedding guests across five functions; a numbered plan is a save. Sunday 12:00 is the biggest slot. Every pairing obeys pages one, three, eight, nine and eleven, so the book closes on its own logic.
posts.claims_check: Figures are Naira Flore couture photos from the site (exhibition look cut-outs and hero_2); captions never say the models wear Naira Petite (their own earrings are too small to read and are cropped out on interior slides). Brushed Gold Huggies 12 mm, no stones; Baguette Huggies Emerald, 18 mm, described as green; Verdant band adjusts US 6-8, rhodium plated, green cubic zirconia not emerald; Marquise Layering Set 40 cm + Y-lariat; Serpentine Whisper Chain Silver 40 + 5 cm, 10 mm cushion, Rhodium Silver Tone Plated. 'Made to measure in Nashik' is said of the outfits only. 'No stones for the haldi to settle in' describes the plain brushed surface, not a stain-proof claim.

risks: Kalam is a fourth face and the brand rule says never add one: the handwritten notes need the owner's sign-off. Better and more Naira: Vandana writes the ~60 short notes by hand in graphite on ivory paper, scanned at 600 dpi and used as images; Kalam is only the stand-in.

The couture photos (look-1..7, hero_1..3) show models wearing their own statement earrings that are not Naira Petite. They appear only as small figures (P12 cover, 352px tall) or cropped below the chin, and no caption says they wear Naira pieces. Confirm with the owner that these outfits and shoots may be used and are current.

On-model jewellery photos (marquise-layering-set/02, baguette-tennis-necklace/04 and /08, toggle-link-chain/02, serpentine silver/01, bold-nocturne-chain/04) are Higgsfield generations already live on the PDPs. Prices drifted three times in October. Prices appear only on index slides and must be re-read from Shopify on the day each post is rendered.
Silk Mesh Cuff width conflict: listing says about 15 mm, an approved ad said 19 mm. The number is kept off the P2 image; confirm before using it anywhere.
Toggle Link Chain clasp: the listing says toggle bar and ring, the brand bible's audit says spring ring with a pavé gate. P3 never describes the clasp; fix the listing.

House rules must stay consistent across pages (thread decides metal, sleeve decides wrist, neckline first, dupatta). QA should check every pairing against pages 1, 3, 9 and 11 before rendering; one contradiction breaks the book's authority.

Karwa Chauth is observed mostly in North India and less in Maharashtra (46% of buyers). P2 keeps it to one object (the chalni) with no fasting or husband framing, and the cuff stands on its own for anyone who does not observe it.
'The card party' (P4, P5) is a common Diwali custom; keep it to the occasion name with no gambling words.

Clutter risk: a notebook can tip into scrapbook soup, which the owner rejected (stickers, stamps, postmarks). Each cover is capped at one swatch or one tool, pins only where something is attached, at most three notes, one pressed sprig in the whole post.
Velista lacks the degree sign, square brackets, rupee sign and middle dot; any 'N°', '[01]', '₹' or '·' set in Velista will fall back and break. Builders must set those in Jost.
Reel covers: changing a cover after posting is unverified; upload the designed 1080x1920 cover at posting. A scheduler may crop 3:4 to 4:5; all masters keep the top and bottom 45px clear.
AI budget: this option uses at most 3 of the ~8 shared Higgsfield elements (AI-1 two textures, AI-2 optional thimble); everything else is SVG or real photography.
